rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Animal behaviour includes reflex actions (automatic, spinal-level responses via a reflex arc), taxes (directional movements: photo-, chemo-, thigmo-, geotaxis), and kinesis (non-directional movement). Social animals form dominance hierarchies (leadership). Fish and birds migrate seasonally to feeding or breeding grounds — a behavioural adaptation.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Reflex arc: Receptor → Sensory neuron → CNS (spinal cord) → Motor neuron → Effector
Taxis: directional movement (positive = toward, negative = away)
Kinesis: non-directional (random) movement in response to a stimulus

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A reflex arc is SHORT (spinal level); it does NOT involve the brain (faster response).  ·  Taxis is DIRECTIONAL (toward/away from a stimulus); kinesis is NON-DIRECTIONAL (random movement).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a clear reflex arc diagram and the distinction between taxis and kinesis.  ·  The four types of taxes (photo-, chemo-, thigmo-, geotaxis) are a common short-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Reflex: touching a hot object → hand withdraws (reflex arc: skin receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → muscle).  ·  Phototaxis: earthworms move AWAY from light (negative phototaxis).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Reflex action: automatic, involuntary; reflex arc (spinal level, no brain).  ·  Taxis: directional movement (phototaxis, chemotaxis, thigmotaxis, geotaxis).  ·  Kinesis: non-directional (random) movement; different from taxis.  ·  Dominance and leadership: social hierarchies in group-living animals.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The fastest reflex is the knee-jerk (patellar) reflex, with a latency of ~30–50 ms.  ·  Some salmon (e.g., Atlantic salmon) migrate thousands of km upstream to spawn in the stream where they were born.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Animal behavior: the actions and responses of animals to stimuli; includes innate (fixed) and learned behaviours.  ·  Reflex action: an automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus, mediated by a reflex arc (receptor → sensory neuron → CNS → motor neuron → effector).  ·  Taxes: orientation responses (movement toward or away from a stimulus). Phototaxis (light), chemotaxis (chemical), thigmotaxis (touch), geotaxis (gravity).

rows.text: Migration is the regular and periodic passing of animals from one place to another place for various purposes.  ·  Migration: seasonal, genetically programmed movement between habitats  ·  Fish migration: seasonal movement to feeding/breeding grounds.
